channel.title: Self-hosting, homelab and DevOps – notes from practice
channel.description: Practical notes by Serge Zabolotny, fullstack & AI developer in Dresden: leaving the cloud with a home server – Proxmox, LXC containers, Nextcloud, Immich – plus access, Tailscale, Cloudflare Tunnel and backups.

item.title: Backup the 3-2-1 way and the restore test: a backup only counts once it has been restored
item.description: Most backup stories end at the same point: the backup ran – but nobody ever tested whether it can be restored. Here is how I back up my Proxmox host and how I test the restore without endangering anything running.

item.title: CRA reporting duty from 11 September 2026: 24 hours, 72 hours, 14 days
item.description: Since 11 September 2026, manufacturers of products with digital elements must report actively exploited vulnerabilities – in three stages and on a fixed clock. What this means for development and DevOps teams.

item.title: How much routine work does AI save? A calculator based on studies
item.description: The studies show very different numbers – from just under 3% to over 40%. Instead of a single number, the calculator gives three scenarios, each with its source, in hours and euros for your team.

item.title: AI Act Article 50: what needs doing by 2 December 2026
item.description: Most of Article 50’s transparency duties have applied since 2 August 2026. For the machine-readable marking of generative AI already on the market, a transition period runs until 2 December 2026. A checklist for developers and operators.

item.title: NIS2 for small IT companies and freelancers: thresholds, deadlines, duties
item.description: The German NIS2 implementation act has been in force since 6 December 2025. Whether a company is directly affected depends on sector and size – but small firms feel it as suppliers too.

item.title: Career change into DevOps in Germany: my plan, my evidence, my gaps
item.description: I am looking for a permanent IT job, with DevOps and platform engineering as the best fit. This is an open account of what the market offers according to the numbers, where I come from and how I make my skills verifiable.

item.title: The world in 10–20 years: three scenarios instead of a forecast
item.description: Nobody knows what the world looks like after AI, robots and drones. What one can do: collect measured numbers, derive scenarios from them and ask what stays the same in all of them – from the view of someone working in IT and DevOps.

item.title: Why I left macOS – and what my 2013 iMac can still do
item.description: An iMac with 32 GB of RAM and a good display is not junk after twelve years. Why I switched to Windows and Linux anyway – a personal field report, not a benchmark.

item.title: Leaving the cloud: a home server instead of Google, iCloud & co.
item.description: At home I run a Proxmox server with 15+ services. Here is which cloud services it replaces for me, what it costs – in time – and where you are better off staying in the cloud.

item.title: Reaching and protecting a home server: Tailscale, Cloudflare Tunnel, vzdump
item.description: A home server is only as good as its access and its backups. My principle: no port forwarding, every access path a conscious decision, a backup every day.

item.title: Proxmox & LXC in a homelab: which containers I run and why
item.description: Four containers, four roles: how my home server is built, which programs run where and how I laid out the storage.

item.title: CI/CD for Next.js 15 on a VPS: GitHub Actions, PM2 reload and Caddy
item.description: Manual deployments were slow and error-prone. Today a git push is enough – no downtime and no PaaS.

item.title: AI content with human-in-the-loop: 200+ guide articles from LLM drafts
item.description: With care law, AI mistakes are not acceptable. This is how I use a language model as a writing aid without handing it the responsibility.

item.title: Zero Trust for the homelab: Cloudflare Tunnel and Access instead of open dashboards
item.description: An internal dashboard was publicly reachable via a subdomain. Here is how I locked it down with Cloudflare Tunnel, Cloudflare Access and Tailscale.
